questions.q: Why do people fail at big goals, per the summary?
a: Working toward them daily for years is hard
They choose goals that are too small
They set too many short deadlines
They lack the natural talent required
questions.why: Lesson 1 says setting a goal is fun, but showing up every day is not.

questions.q: What helps keep motivation up on a long project?
a: Reminding yourself what you are working toward
Rewarding yourself only at the very end
Keeping the goal private from others
Changing the goal whenever it stalls
questions.why: Lesson 1 suggests visible reminders of the goal's purpose.

a: Specific, measurable, attainable, realistic, time-bound
Simple, meaningful, actionable, relevant, timed
Specific, measurable, ambitious, relevant, tracked
Simple, measurable, agreed, realistic, tested
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists the five SMART criteria in full.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest making a book goal measurable?
a: Set a daily page or chapter target
Count the hours spent at the desk
Ask a friend to check progress
Write until inspiration runs out
questions.why: Lesson 2 turns a book goal into a daily two-page draft target.

questions.q: How should you handle predictable distractions?
a: Plan for them before they happen
Ignore them and catch up later
Work longer hours to compensate
Drop the schedule and improvise
questions.why: Lesson 3 says anticipation is the best defence against distraction.
